title: fleet: add burst token pool, autoscaler smoothing, and utilization reporting
author: Asha Menon
description: Motivation: Dedicated fleets need predictable committed throughput but also the ability to absorb short bursts without manual capacity changes. Current autoscaler reacts too quickly to transient load spikes which either overprovisions or throttles latency-sensitive requests. This PR introduces three coordinated changes: (1) a fleet-level burst token pool that allows short lived over-commit up to a configurable budget, (2) smoothing for the autoscaler using an adaptive EWMA to reduce oscillations, and (3) extended utilization reporting and Prometheus metrics so SRE and customers can observe token consumption and true GPU utilization.  Design summary: - Burst token pool: each fleet now maintains a token pool measured in 'tokens' where 1 token ~= 1 request-second at fleet target concurrency. Tokens are refilled at the committed rate and can be consumed when instantaneous load exceeds committed capacity. There are global and per-tenant caps and an eviction policy to avoid token hoarding. Config knobs include --burst-pool-size, --burst-refill-rate, and --burst-per-customer-limit. - Autoscaler smoothing: replace the previous simple moving average with an adaptive EWMA that weights recent samples by variance; this avoids jumping the target replica count when a short spike occurs. New flag: --autoscaler-smoothing-window-ms and --autoscaler-variance-threshold. - Utilization reporting: new Prometheus metrics: redwood_fleet_utilization, redwood_fleet_burst_tokens_total, redwood_fleet_burst_tokens_consumed, redwood_burst_token_evictions, and per-gpu redwood_gpu_active_pct. Metrics include labels for fleet_id, region, and model_family.  Implementation notes: - services/fleet-manager/burst_pool.go: core token pool, refill loop, and eviction. - services/fleet-manager/autoscaler.go: EWMA estimator and integration with scale decision path. - pkg/metrics/registry.go and integrations/prometheus: register new metrics and add dashboards. - cmd/agent: add agent-side accounting to enforce per-customer burst-per-worker limits and to forward token consumption events. - infra/helm: expose new environment variables and defaults for Dedicated customers. - docs/dedicated/autoscaling.md: operational guide, migration steps, knob descriptions, and recommended SLOs.  Migration and rollout: Default behavior preserves existing capacity semantics (burst pool disabled by default for existing fleets). New dedicated customers created after this deploy have a small default burst pool enabled (configurable by account). Rollout plan: canary at 5% fleets for two days, then 50% for one week, then full rollout. Customers can opt-in early via fleet annotation. Operators must run scripts/migrate_burst_tokens.sh to seed historical usage if they want non-empty pools for existing fleets.  Backwards compatibility and safety: - If burst pool is disabled, autoscaler behaves exactly as before. - Token consumption cannot reduce committed throughput; only extends short bursts. - Eviction prevents low-priority or idle tenants from starving active ones — policy documented in docs.  Testing: - unit tests for token accounting and EWMA estimator. - integration e2e test tests/e2e/fleet_burst_test.go simulates step load and validates no oscillation and controlled token use. - load test in benchmark-lab showed 8-12% reduction in 95th percentile latency under bursty workloads with <3% steady-state cost increase.  Observability and alerts: added recommended Grafana panels and Prometheus alert rules (alerts if burst_tokens_consumed > 80% for >10m). Also added runbook entries.  Related work and references: ENG-3127 (autoscaler stability epic), SRE-88 (incident follow-up for over-scaling).

release_notes: Introduce fleet burst token pool (off by default), autoscaler smoothing (configurable), and new utilization metrics. Operators can opt-in and follow docs/dedicated/autoscaling.md for migration. Customers see improved tail latency under bursty traffic with minimal steady-state cost impact.
